About 750 kW of heat is released (exactly 750.3 kW). I checked the arithmetic with a short Python calculation.

The −92 kJ/mol is per mole of reaction as written, and that reaction makes 2 mol of NH3. So it works out to 46 kJ per mol of NH3.

- Molar mass of NH3 = 14.007 + 3 × 1.008 = 17.031 g/mol
- Molar flow = 1,000,000 g/h ÷ 17.031 g/mol ÷ 3600 s/h = 16.31 mol/s
- Heat released = 16.31 mol/s × 46 kJ/mol = 750.3 kJ/s, which is about 750 kW

A common mistake is to apply the full 92 kJ to each mole of NH3. That gives about 1500 kW, twice the correct value.

This assumes the −92 kJ/mol holds at the reactor conditions. It is the standard value near 25 °C, and at real synthesis temperatures (about 400–500 °C) the heat of reaction is somewhat larger in magnitude. I did not correct for that.
